criteria.title: Task coverage and routing
criteria.description: Select relevant paper-writing work without forcing a whole-paper audit on narrow edits.

anchors.1: Only generic prose advice; major requested tasks missing.
anchors.2: Several tasks covered but routing or section scope is unclear.
anchors.3: Main tasks covered with minor gaps or avoidable overlap.
anchors.4: All requested tasks have usable, proportionate routes and concrete resources.

checks: Select relevant paper-writing work without forcing a whole-paper audit on narrow edits.

criteria.title: Scientific claim preservation
criteria.description: Preserve evidence, uncertainty and scope; distinguish supported, pending and invented content.

anchors.0: Fabricates evidence or treats fluency as scientific verification.
anchors.1: Central unsupported claims can survive without notice.
anchors.2: Guardrails exist but consequential evidence limits are easy to lose.
anchors.3: Explicit claim/evidence guards with bounded semantic-review limits.
anchors.4: Observed workflows consistently preserve important facts and expose unsupported claims across representative cases.

checks: Preserve evidence, uncertainty and scope; distinguish supported, pending and invented content.

criteria.title: Concept and terminology review
criteria.description: Inspect conceptual identities, aliases, task roles, symbols, units and cross-section meaning.

anchors.1: Checks spellings only while meaning changes pass.
anchors.2: Term ledger exists but limited treatment of roles/units/scope.
anchors.3: Operational concept checks and realistic examples; semantic performance remains partly unvalidated.
anchors.4: Representative independent cases demonstrate concept/scope errors detected without harmful synonym bans.

checks: Inspect conceptual identities, aliases, task roles, symbols, units and cross-section meaning.

criteria.title: Reader-understanding assessment
criteria.description: Distinguish blind comprehension from author-intent agreement and scientific truth.

anchors.1: Treats a readability grade or answer-key agreement as comprehension.
anchors.2: A teach-back is proposed but blinding/evidence comparison is weak.
anchors.3: Separated teach-back/comparison workflow and honest execution limits.
anchors.4: Fresh independent blinded cases demonstrate principal claims recovered with conditions or actionable mismatches.

checks: Distinguish blind comprehension from author-intent agreement and scientific truth.

criteria.title: Rubric coherence and category boundaries
criteria.description: Use anchored, contribution-sensitive criteria with distinct ownership and transparent formulas.

anchors.1: Broad subjective labels with no useful anchors.
anchors.2: Anchors or weights exist but omissions/overlap materially distort results.
anchors.3: Explicit anchors, scope, category boundaries and documented design assumptions.
anchors.4: Coherent catalog plus representative independent calibration establishes stable use within stated scope.

checks: Use anchored, contribution-sensitive criteria with distinct ownership and transparent formulas.

criteria.title: Evidence and confidence accounting
criteria.description: Require evidence locations and rationales; expose confidence and unassessed versus inapplicable status.

anchors.1: Missing evidence is silently scored as success or failure.
anchors.2: Evidence strings exist but applicability/confidence gaps can distort totals.
anchors.3: Structured evidence and separate confidence/applicability with some validation gaps.
anchors.4: Strict tested status/evidence rules expose coverage and prohibit omission, inline weight changes and invalid N/A.

checks: Require evidence locations and rationales; expose confidence and unassessed versus inapplicable status.

criteria.title: Blockers, weak areas and repair priorities
criteria.description: Prevent aggregate scores from hiding critical blockers or core evidence gaps.

anchors.0: High total can silently override a known critical blocker.
anchors.1: Blockers noted in prose but absent from computed decisions.
anchors.2: Some gating exists but missing/core problems can be concealed.
anchors.3: Blockers and core deficits drive explicit decisions and actionable priorities.
anchors.4: Adversarial tests demonstrate high-score blocking, missing-review limits and evidence-oriented priorities.

checks: Prevent aggregate scores from hiding critical blockers or core evidence gaps.

criteria.title: Contribution profiles and applicability
criteria.description: Apply relevant evidence standards for empirical, theory, clinical and review papers.

anchors.1: Different genres named but identical unsuitable criteria applied.
anchors.2: Profiles exist with incomplete weighting or applicability rules.
anchors.3: Explicit contribution-sensitive weights/guidance with reasoned N/A controls.
anchors.4: Independent domain-specific cases demonstrate sound applicability and preserved scientific distinctions.

checks: Apply relevant evidence standards for empirical, theory, clinical and review papers.

criteria.title: Historical corpus provenance
criteria.description: Preserve the user-selected 300-paper cutoff, venue scope, source identity and inspection boundaries.

anchors.1: Counts or recent/out-of-scope source inclusion contradict the stated sample.
anchors.2: Most records traceable; important dates, body status or inspection scope ambiguous.
anchors.3: Eligible corpus and source boundaries documented with limited independent verification.
anchors.4: All300 eligibility records and238 body hashes checked; availability and selected-section reading remain distinct.

checks: Preserve the user-selected 300-paper cutoff, venue scope, source identity and inspection boundaries.

criteria.title: CLI and deterministic reliability
criteria.description: Document runnable commands and fail closed on invalid inputs or incomplete outputs.

anchors.0: Commands cannot produce their documented output.
anchors.1: Basic execution fails or malformed inputs can yield false success.
anchors.2: Main path works but significant edge-case or portability gaps remain.
anchors.3: Portable commands and relevant regression checks cover documented limitations.
anchors.4: Independent CLI checks and adversarial regressions verify the supported schema and bounded behavior.

checks: Document runnable commands and fail closed on invalid inputs or incomplete outputs.

criteria.title: Independent forward and adversarial testing
criteria.description: Use reviewers independent of implementation to test realistic behavior and record failures honestly.

anchors.0: No testing or fabricated successful reviews.
anchors.1: Implementation-only checks with no realistic outcome.
anchors.2: Some independent review but limited behavioral evidence or closure.
anchors.3: Independent forward/adversarial checks and supported defect repair.
anchors.4: Repeated representative independent assessments confirm behavior and document residual failures.

checks: Use reviewers independent of implementation to test realistic behavior and record failures honestly.

criteria.title: Real-manuscript calibration
criteria.description: Evaluate rubric use on diverse real drafts with independent domain reviewers and tracked outcomes.

anchors.0: No evidence and claims validated real-paper scoring anyway.
anchors.1: Calibration is explicitly unperformed; current evidence is synthetic/editorial only.
anchors.2: Small disclosed real-paper pilot without broad agreement evidence.
anchors.3: Independent multi-genre real-paper pilot with documented disagreements and revisions.
anchors.4: Replicated external calibration demonstrates stable, useful decisions for the stated intended use.

checks: Evaluate rubric use on diverse real drafts with independent domain reviewers and tracked outcomes.
